triggerReason: The public taxonomy treated humans as a strange fourth kind and the dashboard hid durable resource flows behind static-looking projections.
action: Changed the domain and PostgreSQL taxonomy to human, ai and robot; added a checksum-compatible migration and v1 API adapter; introduced deterministic inter-community resource balancing, resource-transfer events and a v2 Observatory contract; redesigned the front door around a city information layer with production, consumption, transfer, inventory and pressure ledgers.
outcome: Release implementation edc426e passed 245 tests including 16 real PostgreSQL/independent-restore checks, 25 Playwright/axe scenarios, zero lint warnings, zero audit vulnerabilities, exact 365-Turn replay with conserved resource transfers, the v2 closure gate and a 10,000-tick stress run. Production deployment and public flow evidence are pending.

metrics.label: Persisted resource rows exposed per Turn

evidence: Resident taxonomy is human, ai and robot in TypeScript, PostgreSQL and Observatory v2
Every transfer is conserved in source and destination ledgers
Every non-zero transfer resource produces an append-only event
Legacy backup taxonomy is normalized only after checksum verification
The city information layer reads the committed Turn rather than a display fixture
Desktop, mobile, Chinese and WCAG A/AA city-flow scenarios pass
Playwright uses an isolated non-reused port so another repository cannot masquerade as this application
Release implementation commit edc426e passed every local and environment-backed gate
